probe.format_note: 16:9 landscape, low resolution (736x414, 1498 frames at 60 fps), single full-frame film, no letterbox. Stereo HE-AAC 44.1 kHz music track at about 120 BPM (bar about 2 s): quiet rising build 0-3.7 s (RMS about -38 dB rising to -14 dB), full beat from about 3.75 s, strong bar downbeats at about 3.75, 5.75, 7.75, 9.75, 11.75, 13.75, 15.75, 19.75, 23.5 s; short breakdowns (dips to about -28 dB) at 5.0-5.6, 9.0-9.7 and 17.0-17.9 s; ends on a sustained hold to 25.0 s, then cuts out.

mode.alt_film_mode: UI when the content package launches software, an app or a dashboard; EXPLAINER-style data beats (one number per scene) fit any package with figures
mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin (owner note): borrow its motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its 3D art pieces, its English card copy or its figures; a voiceover package defaults to REEL, and the reference's own grammar is a sequence of single-number UI cards, which suits number-led reels

ignored.why: all English card copy ('Pie Chart', 'Bar Chart', 'Line Graph', 'Spend', 'Subscribed in a week', 'Announcement', 'New update coming at 2pm.', 'Payment history', 'Essentials', 'Lifestyle', 'Savings & Investments', month and date tick labels) and every figure ('85%', '$105.500', '+25,536', '4.9 ★', '25.500$', '1.255$', '6.845$') are third-party content; never reused as text or numbers — our numbers come only from the content package
the Instagram and X logos on the announcement card are third-party brand marks; never reused (the brand's own handle or logo may take the slot only if the package asks)

the specific 3D art pieces (pink particle sea creature, 3D UI-block city, melting pink cube with blue drops, chrome-purple ribbon, macro petal blur, voxel-cluster grid, desk of geometric drafting tools, tweezer with sprouting green tubes, dark coral/torus/berry still life) are the reference's scenery and subjects; never copied — each of our scenes draws its own subject from the voiceover in this rendering style

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 480 px (5 sheets, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3): cuts at 0.08, 0.33, 0.58, 1.08, 1.33, 1.58, 3.98, 5.48, 6.13, 8.37, 9.33, 12.13, 20.98 s; two further cuts the detector missed (similar grey/blue tones) read from the dense sheets at about 14.45 and 17.2 s, and one inside the teaser at about 0.83 s; dense sheets fps=8 at 240 px over the whole clip (7 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*4 + index*0.125 s); audio RMS per 0.25 s (astats) to place the build, the downbeats and the breakdowns. Spans and move durations are accurate to about ±0.1 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled; the source is low resolution, so fine card text sizes are estimates.

visual_language: A data-card showcase: every scene is one frosted glass UI card holding one idea (a ring, bars, a line, one big number, a notice, a rating, three rows) floating in front of a high-end, colourful 3D art world. Medium: polished 3D renders (glossy, liquid, soft-body, particles, chrome, iridescent and clear glass materials, studio light, very shallow depth of field) with flat, crisp, code-style UI cards composited in real depth. Typography: one clean geometric sans in white — a big bold number as the hero, a small semibold label top-left that types on in one or two steps after the main animation, tiny tick labels; never more than one line of real text per card. Rhythm: a 1.6 s cold-open of 0.25 s flashes, then eleven shots in 25 s; full scenes last about 2.2-4 s (average about 2.6 s); every scene follows the same beat: world alone (about 0.2-0.3 s) → card fades in with backdrop blur (about 0.1-0.25 s) → the data animates (1-1.75 s, slow-fast-slow counting) → label types on → hold (0.5-1.5 s). Cuts land on bar downbeats or inside breakdown dips of a 120 BPM track; the first full scene starts during the quiet build and the beat drops on the second. Moves are smooth and liquid, never snappy: soft fades, slow pushes, organic growth; the only fast motion is the counting middle. Palette changes completely from world to world (pink haze, grey-lilac, beige, magenta on grey, pale grey macro, blue-grey, sage, navy), held together by the identical white-on-glass card. Signature moments: the teaser montage of end frames, the card that stays still while the world behind it swaps, the block that melts behind the chart, the ribbon coiling through the card's depth, liquid that pours and sets into the card, the tool tip that squeezes out the card and a bush of tubes, and the dark three-number finale.
look: Real 3D, not flat: physically lit 3D objects with glossy clearcoat, liquid and soft-body surfaces, chrome and iridescent metals, clear and frosted glass with refraction, particles and volumetric haze; soft studio area light with gentle contact shadows and rim highlights; very shallow depth of field (foreground and background pieces heavily blurred, extreme macro blur in one scene); backgrounds are seamless studio sweeps or soft gradients (pink haze, neutral grey, beige, blue-grey, sage, deep navy with a top glow), no horizon. The UI card is frosted glass: strong backdrop blur and slight colour pickup from what is behind, rounded corners (radius about 6-8% of card width), a thin bright rim, a faint inner highlight, no hard drop shadow; content is pure white; 3D objects pass both behind (blurred through the glass) and in front of the card.
code_translation: Built as real 3D in code, never flattened: three.js scene per world (MeshPhysicalMaterial with clearcoat, transmission, iridescence and roughness for glossy, glass and chrome pieces; tube geometry along animated curves for ribbons and sprouting tubes; noise/vertex displacement for melting and liquid surfaces instead of simulation; instanced meshes for clusters of primitives; points with soft sprites for particle seas; soft area/rect lights plus an environment map; depth of field as a bokeh/blur pass). The glass card is a flat plane inside the same 3D scene (transmission + roughness for frost, or a rendered-target blur sampled behind the card) so objects can pass in front of and behind it; card content (labels, numbers, ring, bars, line) is drawn crisp on top in HTML/SVG with the shaped brand Persian font. Counters roll digit by digit with a slow-fast-slow curve (e.g. easeInOutCubic with a long tail) and Persian digits; labels type on whole words. Low source resolution (736x414) means the target sharpness comes from our build, not from the reference.
continuity: One constant object carries the film: the same frosted glass card style appears in every scene, so wildly different worlds read as one product.
Background swap under a still card: the world behind cuts to a new one while the card keeps its position and content, so the cut reads as a change of context, not a new scene.

The 3D world produces the card: liquid pours and sets into it, a ribbon feeds and flattens into it, UI slabs slide together into it, a tool tip squeezes it out — the card is born from the scene's material.
Depth interleaving: 3D objects pass behind the card (blurred through the glass) and in front of it (sharp), placing the flat card inside the 3D space.
The subject transforms while the data animates: the object melts, sprouts, or gathers in step with the chart or number, so the world reacts to the figure.
Same internal beat in every scene: world alone → card fades in → data animates with a slow-fast-slow count → label types on → hold; repetition makes each new number easy to read.
Cold-open teaser: the end frame of every later scene flashes for 0.25 s at the start, promising the whole sequence before it plays.
Colour world changes at every cut while the card's white-on-glass treatment stays fixed; the last scene turns dark after the light scenes as a finale.
Cuts are placed on bar downbeats or inside the music's breakdown dips; the count's fast middle sits on the full beat.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin (Pinterest, owner note): ADAPT only. Never copy its English card copy, its figures, the Instagram/X logos, its specific 3D art pieces (particle sea creature, slab city, melting pink block, chrome ribbon, petal macro, voxel grid, drafting-tool desk, tweezer and tubes, coral still life) or its shot order one by one.

Source is 16:9 landscape and low resolution (736x414): a 9:16 film rebuilds each composition vertically (card centred in the upper-middle safe zone, 3D world filling the height, depth blur kept); fine text sizes were estimated.

The 3D worlds are high-end renders (liquid, soft-body, particle volumes): in three.js they are approximated (displacement, tubes, instancing, points), not simulated; L5 should pick subjects whose motion stays convincing with these tools and keep render time in check.
Persian text on frosted glass over busy colour: contrast must be checked per scene (white text needs enough frost/dim behind it); readability ranks above the look.

Hold times: data scenes give the number about 0.5-1.5 s after it lands; Persian hold times and minimum sizes win over the pace, and the 0.25 s teaser flashes must carry no text the viewer is expected to read.

Numbers on screen follow references/data-viz.md: every figure comes from the content package with its source, Persian digits and separators, and the counting curve must land exactly on the true value; the reference's charts (ring, bars, line, rows) are motion patterns only.

Direction: the reference reads left to right (bars rise left → right, line draws left → right, labels top-left, icons at the right end): for Persian follow references/rtl-grammar.md (labels top-right, reveals and line draw from the right where meaning allows); type-on reveals whole joined words, never letters.
Reference colours (pink haze, grey-lilac, beige, magenta, blue-grey, sage, navy, coral) map onto brand colour roles and banned colours; the reference's materials, light and depth stay (D55).
The reference has its own music with cuts on its downbeats; our cuts follow the voiceover first, and L6 places accents on our cuts rather than reusing their music.
